transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you, too. Um, well, what brings me in is that my sleep has just gotten really messed up lately. I’ll either stay up half the night with my mind just... running, or I’ll wake up way too early and feel like I never rested at all. It's just really starting to get to me.
When you are lying awake at night, what are the primary thoughts or feelings that keep your mind running?

It's just a bunch of different things all at once, really. My thoughts will just jump around. Like, one second I'm thinking about mortgage payments, and then suddenly I'm stressing over my CPA study schedules, and then my mind is on something totally random like the kitchen cabinets. It just... it all goes so fast that I can’t slow my brain down enough to actually relax.
During these times when your mind is racing, do you feel an unusual sense of energy, euphoria, or irritability, or does it feel more like a sense of worry and tension?

Well, it kind of depends on the day, I guess. It’s not really just worry. Like, earlier in the month, I felt almost... lit up and just unstoppable. I had so much energy. But then that energy kind of turns into being really irritable. I found myself snapping at my mom, or even my supervisor at work, over little questions that normally wouldn’t bother me at all. So, yeah, it's definitely more of an unusual energy and getting annoyed easily rather than just feeling tense.
When you felt that 'lit up' and unstoppable energy, how many days in a row did that feeling last?

Um, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I didn't keep track of exactly how many days it was. It just felt like a stretch of time where I was going non-stop, but... yeah, I couldn't give you an exact number. The days kind of just blur together when I get like that.

During that period where you felt unstoppable, did you notice any significant changes in your behavior, such as taking on many new projects, spending more money than usual, or needing very little sleep?

Yeah, I definitely started doing a lot more. For a while, I just had this huge burst of energy. I'd get home from work and instead of relaxing, I was just... cleaning the whole place, making lists for home renovations, checking interest rates, and even trying to set up ideas for a side-job. It was all happening right after work, and it just felt like I couldn’t shut it off.
Looking back at that stretch of time when you felt unstoppable, would you say that feeling lasted for at least a full week, or was it shorter than that?

I think it was at least a week, yeah. I mean, the really obvious cycling between that charged-up stretch and... and this crash, it's been going on for about a month now. It all really started since the mortgage became real. So it's been a few weeks of just going back and forth like that.
During that period where you felt unstoppable, did you ever feel like you had special powers, or did you hear or see things that other people couldn't?

No, I didn't experience anything like that. I didn't think I had any kind of special powers or anything. And no, I wasn't hearing or seeing things that weren't there. I just had a lot of energy and couldn't stop doing things, but I was still... living in reality, I guess you could say.
During that week or more when you felt unstoppable, was the behavior severe enough that you required hospitalization?

No, I didn't need to go to the hospital. It was intense, and I was doing a lot, but it never got to the point where I needed to be admitted or anything like that. I was still going to work and mostly functioning, just... in overdrive.
